title: Theme Conflict Diagnosis
description: Isolate theme and child-theme issues affecting layout, functionality, or compatibility with plugins and the block editor.

steps.title: Document Layout or Function Breakage
steps.instructions: Capture screenshots of broken pages, list affected templates (single, archive, checkout), and note if the issue appeared after a theme update.

steps.title: Switch to a Default Theme Temporarily
steps.instructions: Activate Twenty Twenty-Four (or latest default) on staging. If the issue disappears, the active theme or child theme is involved.

steps.title: Test Parent vs Child Theme
steps.instructions: Switch from child to parent theme. If the child alone breaks, review functions.php overrides, dequeue scripts, and custom template parts.

steps.title: Review functions.php and Custom Code
steps.instructions: Comment out recent additions in the child theme functions.php. Check for deprecated hooks, removed template tags, or aggressive script dequeuing.

steps.title: Check Page Builder and Theme Integration
steps.instructions: Elementor, Divi, and similar builders can conflict with theme headers/footers. Regenerate CSS, clear builder cache, and test with default theme templates.

steps.title: Update Theme and Clear Caches
steps.instructions: Apply pending theme updates on staging first. Purge page cache, CDN, and browser cache after updating theme or builder plugin versions.

steps.title: Verify Key Templates on Production
steps.instructions: After deploying the fix, test homepage, blog, contact page, and WooCommerce flows if applicable. Confirm mobile and desktop layouts.
